headlines.title: Missed Analog Devices' Rally? Here's What Early Buyers Saw
headlines.summary: If you only glanced at the headlines, Analog Devices’ record Q3 2026 results and another big AI-focused acquisition might look like the whole story. For Analog Devices shareholders, the return over the past year was 61.1%, including dividends. If you were weighing a buy decision back on 2025-11-06, you had to decide whether early talk of robotics, edge AI and higher margins justified that future payoff before any of these later data center windfalls showed up in print.

headlines.title: 47 ETFs Add to Analog Devices (ADI) Holdings on Thursday
headlines.summary: ETFs bought $22.7 million in Analog Devices stock on Thursday, Nov. 5.

headlines.title: Analog Devices Completes Acquisition of Alif Semiconductor
headlines.summary: Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) today announced the completion of its acquisition of Alif Semiconductor. The combination of ADI's leadership across sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity and application software, with Alif's AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors, expands ADI's total addressable market and accelerates innovation across industrial, data center infrastructure, defense, energy, robotics, digital health and wearable applications.

headlines.title: Analog Devices (ADI) Sees $69.7 Million in Net ETF Buying on Nov. 3
headlines.summary: ETFs bought $69.7 million of Analog Devices stock on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

headlines.title: ADI Stock Couldn't Defy Gravity Of Chip Sector For Long
headlines.summary: ADI showed relative strength and bucked the weakness in the chip sector. But we still took our profits quickly while we could.

description: Analog Devices, Inc. engages in the design, manufacture, testing, and marketing of integrated circuits (ICs), software, and subsystems products in the United States, rest of North and South America, Europe, Japan, China, and rest of Asia. It provides data converter products, which translate real-world analog signals into digital data, as well as translates digital data into analog signals; power management and reference products for power conversion, driver monitoring, sequencing, and energy management applications in the automotive, communications, industrial, and consumer markets; and power ICs that include performance, integration, and software design simulation tools for accurate power supply designs. The company also offers amplifiers to condition analog signals; and radio frequency and microwave ICs to support cellular infrastructure; and micro-electro-mechanical systems technology solutions, including accelerometers used to sense acceleration, gyroscopes for sense rotation, inertial measurement units to sense multiple degrees of freedom, and broadband switches for radio and instrument systems, as well as isolators. In addition, it provides digital signal processing and system products for numeric calculations. The company serves clients in the industrial, automotive, consumer, instrumentation, aerospace, defense and healthcare, and communications markets through a direct sales force, third-party distributors, and independent sales representatives, as well as online. The company was incorporated in 1965 and is headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts.
